To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of several indicators based on driver performance is better than the use of a single indicator; the fusion of indicators based on driver’s head and eye movements is better than the fusion of indicators from driver performance;
we have developed a new method for generating ground-truth data based on a supervised KSS, and we have proposed a new fusion of several indicators that outperforms all the single indicators.
the fusion of several indicators is a promising approach for driver drowsiness detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a real-time drowsy driving detection system, based on a fusion of several indicators obtained from a vision-based system and the driver physical and driving skills.
the development of a non-intrusively drowsiness detection system based on the fusion of indicators obtained from ADAS, in order to improve road safety.
the development of new indicators for drowsiness detection and their fusion to improve drowsiness detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fusion of indicators based on driving performance is more effective than those based on driver physical measures.

a combination of indicators based on driver's physical performance, such as head movements, blinking rate, eye closure duration and eyelid movements, and indicators derived from driving performance, such as lane position, lateral acceleration and speed, are the most suitable for real-time drowsy driving monitoring.
the best fusion of the proposed indicators, using our method for ground-trUTH generation, is able to detect the driver drowsiness in a reliable and robust way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion of indicators is better than the single indicators, although the best results are achieved by using a single indicator, which is the one based on the driver head movements.
the fusion of several indicators is a better approach for real time drowsiness detection than single indicators.
we can detect driver drowsiness in real time with a 0.5% false alarm rate and a 100% sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain reliable indicators from ADAS in a simulated environment.
it is possible to obtain robust indicators from a vision system, able to be used for drowsiness detection in simulators and real environments.
it is possible to develop a non-intrusion system for driver drowsiness detection, based on the fusion of optimized indicators from ADAS, in simulated environments.
